chunks: Al-Bazanti narrated from Al-Mashriqi, from Abu Al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: What do you say about a man who claimed that he proposed to a woman, and jokingly she married herself to him while she was joking? Then the woman was asked about that, and she said: Yes.
I said: Is it permissible for the man to marry her? He said: “Yes.”

key_terms.امْرَأَةً: a woman, in the context of a proposed marriage
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِشَيْءٍ: it has no legal effect or standing
key_terms.مَازَحَ: he joked, indicating lack of seriousness
key_terms.مَازِحَةٌ: joking, not intending a serious contract

ai.seo_question: Does a joking marriage agreement count as a valid marriage in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a claimed marriage contract conducted in jest. Imam Abu Al-Hasan عليه السلام states that such a joking exchange has no legal effect, and therefore the man may lawfully marry the woman afterward through a valid marriage contract.
